issues.description: Forward-reference string 'FrameProcessor' on dataclass field with no TYPE_CHECKING import is sloppy and breaks tooling.
issues.detail: The new `service: "FrameProcessor"` field uses a string annotation, but there's no actual `FrameProcessor` import (even under TYPE_CHECKING) in frames.py. That makes the annotation a lie — `get_type_hints()` will explode, IDEs can't resolve it, and dataclass introspection sees a string. Either import it properly under TYPE_CHECKING or type it as the protocol/base it actually needs.

issues.description: Identity check `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` on FrameProcessor relies on default __eq__; fine today, landmine tomorrow.
issues.detail: You're comparing FrameProcessor instances with `==`. That works only because no one has overridden `__eq__`. Use `is` for identity comparison — that's what you actually mean here, and it survives anyone later adding value equality to a processor. One character fix, removes a whole class of future bug.

issues.description: Non-active-service case in push_frame is now silently un-suppressed — behavior change not called out.
issues.detail: Old code dropped every `RequestMetadataFrame`. New code only drops it when `frame.service == active_service`. If a request targeting an inactive service ever reaches this push_frame, it now escapes downstream — previously impossible. Either that's intentional (document it and test it) or it's a latent bug. The PR description doesn't mention this branch at all.

issues.description: Test asserts count but not that `frame.service` actually points at service2.
issues.detail: The new assertion checks `len(request_frames) == 1` but never verifies `request_frames[0].service is self.service2`. The whole point of this patch is targeting a specific service; the test should pin that down. Otherwise a regression where `service=` gets set to the wrong processor passes green.

issues.description: Frame ordering changed from (metadata) to (metadata, then request passthrough) without a test pinning the order.
issues.detail: STTService now pushes `_push_stt_metadata()` and then forwards the `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` downstream. Downstream consumers may care about ordering. There's no test covering what downstream sees in what order, and the changelog doesn't spell out that the request frame is now visible past the switcher's targeted-suppression window.

review.summary: Small, well-scoped rename plus a real semantic change: the request frame now carries a target and gets forwarded by services rather than swallowed. Diff is readable, tests updated, changelog entry present — this is a NEEDS-WORK, not a refuse. Main issues: the new `service` field uses a bare string annotation with no matching import, equality comparison should be identity, and the inactive-service branch of push_frame is now a subtle behavior change with no test. Fix the annotation, switch `==` to `is`, and add a test that asserts the request frame's `service` attribute points at the right processor, and this lands.
